sections.evaluation_comments:
9/8/2026
Dog was at front of kennel when approached; alarm barking; pilo; flagged tail. Settled when treat was presented; spoke softly; took treat; brief tail wagging; no longer alarm barking; allowed leash placement easily at kennel front; exited kennel and immediately demeanor became tense; high flagged tail; pilo all along body; slowly posturing towards dogs in passing on way out. Once in yard handler added extended leash; kept hold of leash and walked around yard with dog as dog marked; urinated; defecated multiple times; did not ease tension in body. Handler kept hold of leash with slack as dog sniffed yard; not responsive to coaxing with voice or treats. Dog would walk past assistant handler who was sitting on bench; sniffed near feet for prolonged time; disengaged and walked away. Dog would walk behind bench and take treat from assistant handler; spit out. Handler crouched low and dog approached with brief tail wag; mouth slightly open; took treat; did not sniff hand offered. Dog was not signaling pro-social behaviors during evaluation and focused on marking and sniffing ground; some saliva collecting on mouth. Handler walked dog to exit gate; placed clip leash while dog was distracted at gate; no reaction; would walk up to kennel threshold but didn't enter; neighboring dogs all closed inside; pulled away from kennel; light panting; handler followed dog around and would try again a few times, offering treat scatter; not interested. Assistant handler opened guillotine so dog could see inside portion of kennel; dog would hesitate to enter but slowly entered willingly; removed leash using clip lead.
9/7/2026
Handler approached front kennel, dog was eating. Dog looked up and began alarm barking at handler, handler tossed treat over and reapproached from back kennel. Handler was able to lure dog into back kennel with treats and lower guillotine. Dog again alarm barked and pounced towards handler. Dog then began pawing at gate. Handler offered more treats dog was not interested. Handler prepared large loop and began leashing attempts. Handler grazed leash along dogs back and dog tensed up and turned around. Handler then was able to cast leash over head. Once leash was secure handler opened gate and held leash taut. Handler made sure to hold arm out as dog exited, dog walked out with slow tense posture, pilo and glared at handler. Handler walked dog to PY, dog urinated on a bush in passing. Once in PY Dog remained tense with tail flagged, no signs of softening. Handler kept dog on leash and walked around PY allowing dog to lead. Dog stayed at end of leash, never allowing slack or approaching handler. Handler tossed a few treats out and dog ate them. Dog defecated and continued to walk with tense posture. Handler decided to return dog after about 5 minutes due to FAS. Handler was able to quickly reach and place clip leash. Dog walked slowly back to kennel and hesitated at entrance. Handler tossed in treats and used light leash pressure to guide in. Dog entered and handler used clip leash for leash removal.
9/6/2026
dog stood at front, mild tension, froze as handler reached down, wide eyes, leaned forward and sniffed handler, furrowed brow, lip licked and turned head away, leaned back with lifted front paw then backed up and laid down on bed. Requesting full evaluation

Dog was lying at front of kennel when handler approached, stoic face. Handler knelt down and pulled out hotdogs, dog stood and faced kennel gate, slightly grabby taking hotdogs through bars. Closed outside for AM cleaning, curled up at the back of kennel. Unable to coax forward verbally or with treats, ate treats tossed nearby. Averted gaze when presented with leash and turned away from handler, able to step in and place leash with large loop. Handler positioned taxi directly in front of dog, entered without assistance, rode well to small yard, allowed light petting on head. Dog remained in taxi, scanning surroundings, whale eyed, lip licking. Handler tossed treats in and around taxi, dog remained frozen, ignored treats, began trying to climb further back into taxi. Handler approached, cowered slightly and lip licked but allowed more pets, sniffed treat offered by hand but didn't take. Handler picked up leash, dog once again turned and tried climbing further back into taxi. Rode back to kennel with no issues, hesitant to enter kennel, resisted and bit leash when trying to guide in, handler stepped in kennel, able to guide dog in with mild leash pressure, held leash taut to preview dog from exiting, slowly removed leash by hand.
9/7/2026
Outside for AM cleaning laying at front of kennel with tense body, hard staring handler, stoic, grabby with treats offered. Retreated to back corner of kennel and pancaked when leash was presented, able to slowly approach and place large loop over dogs head with no issues, slight thrashing then exited kennel quickly before freezing alongside neighboring kennel, trembling tense body, lip curling towards dog in kennel, when adjust taxi dog would begin thrashing, became erratic and thrashed self into taxi then settled, rode fine to small play yard. Once in yard dog exited taxi quickly and pancaked in front of handler as handler sat on bench, eyes shifting in all directions, tolerant of petting on head and body but did not seek out attentions, skin crawling when touched on body. When handler got up dog quickly retreated to corner of yard and pancaked, trembling body, heavy panting, eyes wide and scanning surroundings, very timid and wary of environment. Let dog have a few moments, not interested in treats or coaxing, whale eye and stiff bodied when approached. Placed taxi near dog while picking up leash, dog dashed into taxi on own. No reaction towards clip leash being placed. Rode fine back to kennel, hesitant to exit taxi, would quickly exit taxi but runs back into taxi when leash pressure is felt, tipped taxi over and dog became erratic, spinning around handler resisting entering kennel, able to contain dog into kennel with leash pressure while closing door, used clip leash for leash retrieval.
9/2/2026
walked on ramp, nervous with handler and others around, flinched with touching around neck - noticed during attempt to place mylar, moderate restraint - leash muzzle for vaccines, resists leash handling, allows some handling, does not allow much petting, transported to kennel with pet taxi

sections.evaluation_comments:
9/13/2026
Outside for AM cleaning with tense body, tail tucked but becoming flagged as handler approached, head lowered and furrowed brow, very timid at front of kennel. Slowly came forward to accept treat gently but started to back away, froze in place as door was opened, no issues placing large loop leash over head. Exited with easy leash pull, startled by reactive dogs in passing, tail tucked, flinches when startled, walked closely to handler but some hard staring when bumping into handlers leg, no issues walking to small play yard. Once in yard dog was distant from handler all of evaluation, side eyeing, went potty and only ate treats tossed near, would not follow treat trail to handler, mostly slow pacing near play yard exit beginning to heavy wide mouth pant. Will sniff handler and accept treats if approached but will slowly pace away from handler, wary of handler extending hand out to pet, did not allow petting all of evaluation, some whale eye and flinching away. Let dog have a few moments, followed handler to exit and wary of clip leash being attached but allowed it. Slow, easy leash pull back to kennel. Walked into kennel on own, used clip leash for leash retrieval.
9/12/2026
Dog was at front of kennel when approached; head low; slouched over; furrowed brow. Handler spoke softly and offered treats; ate; remained in place with worried expression; relaxed musculature but stress signals present. Dog perked up slightly with leash; ears up; stood up; wary of leash; would back away and hard stare at leash with furrowed brow; lured with treats; able to drape large loop overhead after a minute; dog shifted weight back and cowered; exited kennel with rounded body; tail tightly tucked; ears pinned straight back; pilo along neck and back. Dog kept tense posture up until we reached the yard; non reactive to any dogs in passing; startled heavily when handler tightened stopper on leash whipping head. Once in yard handler added extended leash; dog was avoidant; tail slowly untucked; neutral; began soft panting; drooling; urinated. Dog would eat treats tossed but would not approach handler for treats or coaxing; remained neutral panting at exit gate. Handler was able to grab leash; dog approached handler with tense body; pilo; walked behind handler; nervous; slowly reached for leash stopper while dog was distracted at gate; mild pull back to building; attached clip lead while dog was distracted; no reaction to dogs in passing; retreated into kennel willingly; removed leash with clip lead; took treats from hand through kennel.
9/9/2026
Dog did not eat day 1
9/8/2026
dog reactive in lobby, outside stiff body, not seeking any attention, very stoic, allowed muzzle wrap with mild restraint vaccines given, walked to kennel

Soft wiggly body on approach of kennel, easy leash placement. K9 walks well on leash. K9 is potty trained so took out to play yard to potty. K9 urinated for a long time and defecated 3 times. Walked well back to clinic. K9 was held in hug restraint with muzzle placed (this was only as precaution due to area where sutures were being removed) k9 had no reaction to lower eye-lid suture removal. K9 wagged tail entire interaction. Once suture removal was done, muzzle removed. K9 got zoomies in clinic, played fetch with toys. Allowed e-collar replacement with no issues. Seeked attention from mulitple handlers, jumped up for attention but was verbally corrected without issue. Easy return to kennel, leash removed by hand.
9/13/2026
Dog was standing @ kennel gate with a relaxed body while demand barking.  Presented leash & leashed over e-collar without issues.  Walked with a moderate pull on leash to J-yard.  Would have a long shake off of body then would explore PY with nose to ground.  Would jump up then start to muzzle punch handlers stomach with a closed mouth, handler was able to straight arm leash while waiting for dog to settle then dropped leash.  Dog would jump up then start to muzzle punch towards assistant handlers body, handler was able to pick up leash & walk dog away.  Dropped leash once dog would settle, dog would approach handler, allowed petting on side of body, would again start to jump up.  Handler would pick up leash as dog would jump up & push off against handlers body, dog would start to air snap towards leash not making contact of leash.  Once dog would settle, handler would walk dog out of PY while having a moderate pull on leash back to building.  Entered into S-wing & into kennel room without issues.  Entered into kennel & allowed handler to remove leash by hand without issues.
9/12/2026
Handler was asked to move dog to S wing. Dog was standing with front two on window demand barking at staff standing outside of room not engaging with dog. Handler approached and spoke to dog; dog got off window and stood on floor; could see tail nub wagging; stopped barking; panting and drooling. Handler cracked open door and allowed dog to sniff leash; no reaction; tried placing large loop over cone with door mostly closed but unable to; used sort board only as a way to block doorway so handler could leash without dog dashing out. Once leashed, dog exited room with mild pull; followed handler down hallway; mild pull on leash down hallway; bumping into walls and floor with cone; attached clip lead; entered into new kennel with no issue; removed leash using clip lead; got stuck for a moment on cone but dog stood patiently at door.
9/11/2026
When closing the building for the night handler and second handler cracked open the door, dog was low growling, handler then shut door and dog was growling through window. Had another handler come and pulled the dog and was friendly with them, as soon as dog came out dog was thrashing and lip curled at handler, handler then tried to use light leash pressure dog was observed air snapping at handlers hand.
9/3/2026
Neutral body and tail as handler approached, not interested in treats offered but came forward to sniff handler with some wagging tail. Allowed for easy leash placement at front of kennel over e-collar, exited with easy leash pull, wary of surroundings and startled by reactive dogs in passing on way to "J" yard but once away from dogs and approaching parking lot dog shook off, had soft body and wagging tail rest of way to yard. Once in yard dog began urinating for a long duration of time before coming to handler for attentions with wiggly body and wagging tail, some high energy, allowed petting all over. Some jumping up onto handler but easy to direct off, would follow handler to chair and begin leaning in for pets, accepting pets all over. A little grabby with treats. Followed handler around yard with soft body throughout, solciits attentions whenever handler stops. Easy return to kennel, startled by reactive dogs in passing, walked into kennel on own and allowed handler to remove leash by hand.
9/1/2026
canine was at front of kennel opened kennel and was able to leash easily walked to clinic with no issue. canine allowed handler to pick up and place on scale. walked into clinic surgery kennel with no issue was able to remove leash by hand with no issues. while sedating for surgery light restraint was used and canine had no reaction to injection
8/30/2026
Lying quietly with stoic body.  Not responsive to verbal coaxing or treats.  Slowly retreated to back half of kennel with body lowered.  Requesting a full evaluation.
8/28/2026
Soft calm body, allowed all handling, walked on leash to truck.
8/28/2026
walks on leash, allows all handling and petting, light restraint for vaccines, soft body, slightly timid, takes treats gently

What is the reason for surrender?
PER SOURCE, ASSISTED LIVING IS NOT THE BEST SITUATION FOR THIS DOG THAT HAS LIVED HIS ENTIRE LIFE UNTIL 11 MONTHS AGO IN A HOUSE WITH A LARGE YARD.  THE CONFINED SPACE WAS HARD ON THE DOG, THE AGING OWNER IS UNWELL AND IT WAS VERY HARD ON HER TO KEEP THE DOG AT THE FACILITY.  NO YARD AND THE MANAGER WAS NEVER PLEASED TO HAVE HIM THERE, THEY WERE CONFINED TO A BEDROOM UNLESS LEASHED TO GO OUT.
How long have you had your pet?
10+ YEARS
Where did you get this animal from?
BREEDER. ATTEMPTED TO RETURN PET TO THE BREEDER, NO REPLY.
Is your pet spayed/neutered?
NEUTERED
Is this animal currently showing any signs of illness, taking any medication, or has the animal been diagnosed with a medical or behavioral condition?
HE HAS HAD VALLEY FEVER, TAKEN ANTI FUNGAL OFF AND ON FOR SEVERAL YEARS.  SKIN AILMENTS FROM ALLERGIES.
We offer resources such as low-cost veterinary care, trainers, food/medication coupons, and financial assistance. Would you like any resources instead of surrendering?
NO

YES, IN THE HIGH STRESS SITUATION AT THE ASSISTED LIVING FACILITY, BIT DOWN ON THE OWNERS ARM WHEN OWNER WAS TRYING TO HOLD PET DOWN TO DRESS HIM.

NO, THE BITE BROKE THE SKIN.  JUST ONE BITE ON THE LOW ARM, WRIST AREA.
Do you have pictures of injuries/bites?
NO
Did the bite occur within the last 10 days? Date of bite?
AUGUST 31

NO, HE WILL GROWL A WARNING IF SOMETHING IS AMISS, BUT NOT AGGRESSIVE.
Has the animal ever seriously injured or caused the death of another animal?
NO
How is the animal around children?
HE HAS BEEN AROUND CHILDREN OF ALL AGES (0-ADULT) AND WITH SUPERVISION AND RESPECT, HE LIKES KIDS.  HE SPENT AN EXTENDED STAY, MORE THAN 3 WEEKS WITH A PET SITTER AT HER HOUSE.  SHE HAS 2 DOGS AND 5 CHILDREN AGE 2-11.  A4060980 WARMED UP TO ALL BUT ONE OF THE DOGS.  AND THEY KEPT THEM SEPARATED.

CAUTIOUS AND THEN LOVING.  IT TAKES HIM TIME TO WARM UP TO ANYONE, AND IF GREETED RAPIDLY OR WITH ROUGH PLAY HE WILL RETREAT AND POSSIBLY GROWL.  IF GIVEN A PERIOD OF TIME TO COME TO SOMEONE AND WARM UP, HE WILL CHOOSE IF AND WHEN

70+ WOMAN, 80+ MAN.  GRANDCHILDREN INTERMITTENT 2-18

Cats?
YES, IGNORES THEM
Dogs?
TAKES TIME TO WARM UP TO THEM

UNKNOWN

IGNORES THEM.  THERE WERE TORTOISES, A BIRD AND A CAT.  HE HAS BEEN AROUND MANY SMALL ANIMALS.
Resource Guarding: Describe any known guarding of food, toys, people, or space?
HE WAS THE ONLY DOG IN THE HOUSE, NO RESOURCE GUARDING

YES
Is your pet potty trained?
YES
Familiar with a dog door?
YES
Crate trained?
YES
Leash trained?
YES! VERY GOOD ON WALKS

BASIC SIT, STAY (SOMETIMES) BUT VERY SMART AND COULD LEARN MORE WITH TRAINING

INSIDE, WITH A DOG DOOR TO A LARGE YARD UNTIL THE OWNER WENT TO ASSISTED LIVING THEN NO YARD ONLY WALKS OUTSIDE ON A LEASH SEVERAL TIMES A DAY

NO

MOBILE VET VISIT JANUARY 2026

MODERATE.  HE WAS VERY HIGH ENERGY AS A YOUNG DOG, MORE MELLOW WITH AGE

HE DOES NOT LOVE BATHS OR NAIL TRIMS

WALKS AND LAYING IN THE HOT SUN
